title: Why You Should Take Your Time The First Few Weeks Of School eks-of-school/
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Linsin advises teachers not to rush the beginning of the school year just because colleagues seem to be moving faster into curriculum, group work, or centers. He explains that students' initial eagerness can mask their lack of readiness for full routines, and that unexpected disruptions—like hallway chaos on the way to lunch—are normal and not evidence of a bad class or poor teaching. Rather than reacting with discouragement, he frames such moments as opportunities to prove that the teacher means what they say, by slowing down, backing up, and reteaching expectations precisely. The article closes with an extended metaphor encouraging teachers to hold high standards patiently, since a deliberate early pace pays dividends of ease later in the year.
points: Avoid rushing to match colleagues who seem further ahead in curriculum or student independence early in the year.
Students' early eagerness to please can mask that they are not yet ready to fully execute routines under real conditions.
An early breakdown in behavior (e.g., a chaotic hallway) is normal and doesn't mean the class or the teacher is failing.
Missteps are opportunities to prove consistency—back up, slow down, and reteach the routine rather than lowering expectations.
Once students learn the teacher 'means what they say,' the rest of the year becomes far easier.
quotes: No matter what you hear from your colleagues, no matter how far they say they’ve gotten into the curriculum, or how they’re already working in groups or rotating students through centers, avoid the temptation to join them.

It pays, you see, to get it right the first time around. It pays to take a deliberate approach, to teach the details, the ins and outs, and the A to Zs of being a polite, successful, and contributing member of your classroom.
You watch aghast as your students begin stepping out of line to goof and jostle with their friends, shout out to little brothers or big sisters, and disrupt the working classrooms lining the hallway.
Because early in the school year an occasional breakdown in behavior is expected. No teacher escapes the first few weeks without being tested or tried or disappointed.
Once you convince your class that when you say it they can take it to the bank, everything becomes much, much easier.
Hold them to it and they’ll learn. Take them back to the scene of the crime and give them a chance to fix it and they will.
